verses.text: In Caesarea, there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in the Italian Regiment.
He was devout and honored God with everyone in his household. He gave generously to people in need and prayed to God regularly.
About the ninth hour, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God come to him and call, “Cornelius!”
Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?” The angel said, “Your prayers and gifts to people in need have come before God as a memorial.
Now send men to Joppa and bring back Simon, also called Peter.
He’s staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is beside the sea.”
When the angel left, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier who served him regularly.
He explained everything to them and sent them to Joppa.
The next day, while they were traveling and getting close to the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray. It was around noon.
He got hungry and wanted something to eat. While the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet coming down. It was lowered to the ground by its four corners.
Inside were all kinds of four-legged animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
A voice said to him, “Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.”
Peter answered, “No, Lord! I’ve never eaten anything ordinary or unclean.”
The voice spoke to him a second time: “Don’t call anything unclean if God has made it clean.”
This happened three times. Then the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
Peter was trying to figure out what the vision meant when the men sent by Cornelius arrived. They had asked where Simon’s house was and were now standing at the gate.
They called out and asked whether Simon, also called Peter, was staying there.
While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Spirit told him, “Look, three men are asking for you.
Get up, go downstairs, and go with them without hesitation. I sent them.”
Peter went down to the men and said, “I’m the one you’re looking for. Why have you come?”

They said, “Cornelius the centurion sent us. He’s a righteous man who honors God, and the whole Jewish nation speaks well of him. A holy angel told him to invite you to his house and listen to what you have to say.”
Peter invited them in and gave them a place to stay. The next day he left with them, and some believers from Joppa went along too.
The day after that, they reached Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had gathered his relatives and close friends.
When Peter came in, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and worshiped him.
Peter pulled him up and said, “Stand up! I’m only a man too.”
As they talked, Peter went inside and found many people gathered there.
He said to them, “You know it is considered unlawful for a Jewish person to associate with or visit someone from another nation. But God has shown me I must not call anyone ordinary or unclean.
That’s why I came without arguing when you sent for me. So, why did you ask me to come?”
Cornelius said, “Four days ago, at this very hour, I was fasting. At the ninth hour I prayed in my house. Suddenly, a man in bright clothing stood in front of me
and said, ‘Cornelius, God has heard your prayer. Your gifts to people in need have been remembered before him.
Send to Joppa for Simon, also called Peter. He’s staying at the seaside home of Simon the tanner. When he comes, he’ll speak to you.’
So I sent for you right away, and it was good of you to come. Now we are all gathered here before God, ready to hear everything God has commanded you to say.”
Peter began: “Now I really understand that God doesn’t show favoritism.
In every nation, anyone who honors God and does what is right is welcomed by him.
God sent his message to the people of Israel, announcing peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of everyone.
You know what happened throughout Judea, starting in Galilee after John preached about baptism:
God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power. Jesus went around doing good and healing everyone oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.
We are witnesses to everything he did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a tree.
But God raised him on the third day and allowed people to see him—
not everyone, but witnesses God had chosen beforehand: us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
Jesus commanded us to preach to the people and testify that God appointed him as judge of the living and the dead.
All the prophets testify about him: everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”
While Peter was still saying these things, the Holy Spirit came upon everyone listening to the message.
The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had also been poured out on Gentiles.
They heard them speaking in other languages and praising God. Then Peter said,
“Can anyone refuse to baptize these people with water? They’ve received the Holy Spirit just as we have.”
So he ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.
